From 47b7360ce563e18c524ce92b55fb4da72b3b3578 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Date: Sat, 8 Sep 2018 12:07:26 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] x86/apic/vector: Make error return value negative

activate_managed() returns EINVAL instead of -EINVAL in case of
error. While this is unlikely to happen, the positive return value would
cause further malfunction at the call site.

Fixes: 2db1f959d9dc ("x86/vector: Handle managed interrupts proper")
Signed-off-by: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org

diff --git a/arch/x86/kernel/apic/vector.c b/arch/x86/kernel/apic/vector.c
index 9f148e3d45b4..7654febd5102 100644
--- a/arch/x86/kernel/apic/vector.c
+++ b/arch/x86/kernel/apic/vector.c
@@ -413,7 +413,7 @@ static int activate_managed(struct irq_data *irqd)
 	if (WARN_ON_ONCE(cpumask_empty(vector_searchmask))) {
 		/* Something in the core code broke! Survive gracefully */
 		pr_err("Managed startup for irq %u, but no CPU\n", irqd->irq);
-		return EINVAL;
+		return -EINVAL;
 	}
 
 	ret = assign_managed_vector(irqd, vector_searchmask);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `arch/x86/kernel/apic/vector.c`**
- The return value of the function `activate_managed()` has been modified. Specifically, the line that previously returned `EINVAL` (a positive error code) has been changed to return `-EINVAL` (a negative error code). This change ensures that the function returns a negative value in case of an error, which is the expected convention for error handling in the codebase.

### Relationships
The modification in `vector.c` addresses a potential issue where returning a positive error code (`EINVAL`) could lead to further malfunctions at the call site. By changing the return value to a negative code (`-EINVAL`), the patch aligns the error handling with standard practices, thereby improving the robustness of the code and preventing possible misinterpretations of the error state. This change is linked to a previous commit that aimed to handle managed interrupts properly, indicating that the fix is part of a broader effort to ensure correct error reporting in the interrupt management system.
